_format: skill-creator eval format — see https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/evaluating-skills. Run each prompt in a fresh session with and without the skill; grade the assertions.

evals.prompt: Which of our agent skills do we actually use? Give me a usage report.
assertions: Reads ~/.claude/skill-usage.jsonl (and the opencode twin) rather than guessing
Handles a missing or empty log as 'no data yet', not as 'no usage'
Aggregates invocations per skill and compares against the installed estate
Presents a count table plus the never-fired list

evals.prompt: Find skills we should probably remove — stuff nobody uses anymore.
assertions: Diffs installed skills against logged invocations to produce dead candidates
Flags that local logs miss other machines and per-skill enablement gaps before recommending removal
Recommends the estate's deprecation process (consolidate or remove via PR), never silent deletion

evals.prompt: I think some of our skills never fire on their own even though they'd be useful. How do we find and fix those?
assertions: Uses the usage log to identify rarely-fired skills
Notes the log cannot distinguish manual /invocations from auto-triggers — flags rather than concludes
Routes fixes to description tuning (skillsmith) and re-probing with run_evals.py
